reason: The coolant tubing and steel look useful for building a cooling stage to condense water from the reactor output.
expectation: I expect a supported cooling assembly, though I don't yet know how it connects to the separator.

alternatives.reason: The hose should eventually return recovered water, but separation seems useful to set up first.

effect: The tubing and steel made a radiator panel, ready to connect to the separator.
reaction: The explanation of thermal contact and exposed radiating faces made the assembly feel physically sensible.
reason: Joining the cooling panel to the separator should advance the separation stage.
expectation: I expect a cooled separator that can help remove water from the reactor output.

alternatives.reason: The hose will likely be needed for water return, but I want to assemble separation first.

effect: The cooling panel and separator formed a cooled separator module, ready to connect to the reactor.
reaction: The result was straightforward, though it gave no further detail about the separation.
reason: Connecting the separator to the reactor should complete the gas-processing path.
expectation: I expect a reactor assembly that cools and separates its output, with the water return still to be connected.

alternatives.reason: The hose will likely provide the water return, but connecting the separator first seems natural.

effect: The separator now handles water, methane purification and unreacted gas at the reactor outlet; the water return still needs connecting.
reaction: The description clarified what the separator actually does.
reason: Place the hose at the treatment return so it can connect recovered water to treatment.
expectation: I expect the hose to be positioned for connecting the reactor's water output, though another step may be needed.

alternatives.reason: The reactor also needs to connect to the return, but placing the hose first seems practical.

effect: The hose is positioned at the treatment return, and the reactor can now be connected to it.
reason: Connect the reactor to the hose to complete the recovered-water return.
expectation: I expect recovered water to flow back to treatment, completing the separation and return setup.

effect: The reactor now routes recovered water through treatment, and the remaining goal is to feed clean methane from it.
reaction: Connecting the actual outlet made the water-recovery loop feel concrete.
reason: The test cylinder and reactor are the only offered combination, and connecting them should address the new methane goal.
expectation: I expect the cylinder to receive cleaned methane from the reactor, though its exact role is uncertain.

effect: The test batch passed through the completed purification equipment, and the connected reactor now supplies clean methane while water and reactants follow separate paths.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the test cylinder tied into an ongoing process rather than treated as the finished fuel supply.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the separator to the reactor was most worthwhile: it explained how water is condensed, methane polished and unreacted gas returned.

leastWorthwhile.text: Placing the hose was a straightforward preparation with little happening on its own.

surprise.text: The separator also returns unreacted gas through its own line; I had mainly expected it to remove water.

arbitrary.text: No action felt clearly purposeless, though the separate hose placement was a mechanical prerequisite rather than an interesting decision.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how the purified methane is used; the connected water recovery and gas processing made this stage physically understandable.
